name: How do I prepare for a kitchen demo in a lived-in home?

mainEntity.name: How do I prepare for a kitchen demo in a lived-in home?
mainEntity.text: How do I prepare for a kitchen demo in a lived-in home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Preparing for kitchen demolition in a lived-in home starts with removing everything from cabinets, drawers, and countertops, then moving dishes, food, and appliances into storage or a temporary kitchen area. Homeowners should coordinate with the contractor on water, gas, and power shutoff dates if needed, and clarify where debris will be carried so the rest of the house stays protected. Furniture, flooring, and nearby rooms should be covered or shielded with dust barriers. It also helps to label boxes and keep essentials accessible so daily life is not completely disrupted. Pets and children should be considered in the safety plan because demolition creates noise, dust, and frequent entry and exit. Good preparation reduces damage, speeds up the first phase of construction, and makes the transition into the remodel much easier.
acceptedAnswer.description: Clear the kitchen completely, set up a temporary cooking area, protect adjacent rooms, and confirm utility shutoff dates with the contractor. Pack fragile items, label stored contents, and decide where dust barriers and debris routes will go. Good preparation reduces stress and avoids damage outside the work zone.
